subject: CIP Application
comment: Hello, I was unable to speak during the meeting tonight due to technical issues. I would like to state my position that I mentioned in my comment. My name is Daniela Diebenedetto and I am a concerned neighbor who submitted an application for Taufer park to be reimagined and updated for the neighborhood and surrounding areas. Currently the park is unsafe due to many issues and has been a problem for years with the homeless using and abusing the park. On a daily basis I see drug deals, public urination, physical and verbal fights, littering, trespassing and so much more. I often do not feel safe to go walk or take my children to enjoy the dirt lot grass. I have a recording on my home video camera of my home being vandalized by a homeless man and someone stealing my mail. Also, no cameras I can see in the park area. There is not adequate lighting so crimes are happening in my back yard at 4pm. I am a single 25 year old women living alone. I've called Salt Lake Police for over 6 years now, and it's reached a point where I no longer feel they will come in a timely manner. Not only have I had to install my own home nuisance tame anymoer. this park is a major safety issue for the neighborhood. Taufer Park is not safe and not usable for the neighbors, kids, or tourism visiting our beautiful city. Neighbors have told me of people having sex at all hours of the day an a daily basis, watching the health department clean up poor litter, used needles, and abandoned shopping carts. If this park were fixed then connecting the neighborhood to liberty park and other attractions downtown would be wonderful. The neighborhood children need a safe place to play and access to play equipment. A proper West Park and I see how great that worked to deter the homeless, imagine Taufer Park being a place where farmers markets are held, or food trucks can come and people can actually enjoy the space safely. I truly believe if we can clean up this community can enjoy this space safely. I am open to any ideas and I am willing to work with the city in making the Taufer Park revamp happen. Thank you for your time and consideration. Daniela Diebenedetto.

subject: Dangerous Drivers
comment: I support the neighborhood speed limit from 25 mph to 20 mph on 700 South to address the real problems, namely people driving drunk or impaired by drugs. It seems to me that you made this reduction as a knee-jerk reaction to general fatal accident trends, but such reduction doesn't necessarily address the underlying public and priveleges that you were "doing something." However, in virtually all of these fatal crashes the drivers were drunk or impaired, and it is unlikely that such a small reduction in speed limit will make much of a difference. That said, I believe to something as "trivial" as the speed limit. So clearly the thing to do is to take measures to get those drivers off the streets and to keep them off. Measures such as immediate license revocation and vehicle impoundment upon arrest. And allow no bail penalties for driving without a valid license, proper monitoring of people out on parole or bail, no bail or release for drivers arrested for reckless causing serious injury or fatalities, including immediate notification of parole and probation authorities, and so on. I know much of this is outside to the city council's purview, but you could work with the state legislature and the courts to get stiffer laws. Also, the state could surely enact laws allowing and encouraging the use of speed cameras than that one being wasted on changing speed limit signs. Please don't punish all drivers, most of whom are law abiding and sober, by forcing everyone to drive at horse and buggy speeds. Thank you.

subject: Traffic Issues
topic: D7 Residents owners in sugarhouse/highland drive area proposal
comment: Hello Amy, As a citizen who lives in Sugarhouse and specifically adjacent to South Highland Drive, it's always been somewhat of a bother that most cars are parked on one side of the street. I live on the far east side of Highland Drive, and am somewhat of an issue to urban areas but I have an idea that might work to help it. Basically with the very being decided against I thought that perhaps implementing something similar to alternating sides of the street parking as it is seen other urban areas. Unreachable blockages might be helpful, I grew up with what were called "Traffic Mirrors" or "Broadcast Mirrors" during my teen years spent in Ireland and they have proven to be invaluable tools for helping drivers see around blind corners. Some of these positioned at corners entering onto S Highland Drive from lanes such as Parkway, East Wilmoth Avenue, and Whitlock could go a long way towards reducing the high volume of accidents and close calls we get here. I think we are digging a post hole and putting in a new steel pole for it or attaching to already existing infrastructure. I'd be willing to canvas for this and to see how many are supportive of the idea. Let me know if there's any interest in exploring this. Best Regards, thank you for your time, Grant Murphy

Dear City Council Representatives, I wanted to register a public comment regarding 1850 W Indiana Avenue rezoning. I live at 1834&1810, near the proposed site for the Geller Salt Village, and I am opposed to this rezoning. I do believe that there needs to be increased shelters and services for people experiencing homelessness, but I strongly oppose this location for such a project as it would cause harm and completely change our area. Services like this are always dumped on the west side. It is not fair to this neighborhood, which already struggles with noise and crime issues stemming from I-15, the homeless encampments, and the shelter that already makes walking on the Jordan Parkway feel feel unsafe, and this project will multiply this issue. I believe in creating safe spaces for people to live in, but really question if placing a shelter directly across from a children's playground is safe for both. I am larger than I believe is reasonable to add to an area of this size. Introducing 400+ homes to this community will create a major shift in the neighborhood. Even just the increase in traffic alone would be alarming. This location has a single entrance, and would be a better option, in my opinion, that hundreds of people packed into a small area near our home cannot provide for the best outcome. As a recent neighbor of this area, this project seems like it will harm our neighborhood and something we can do as neighbors to stop this. Thank you for your time. Aubrey Rehmeida
